note: Groups M and T of the 2026-11-21 prose A/B round 2. T cuts the console designer's trap list to one line per trap under a pointer to the preloaded dotnet-hosted-services (the why and the code shape live there) and cuts, in all ten designers, the restatements of task-design: the 'Challenge every piece of scope' and 'defer anything not yet proven necessary' clauses of the Design lean bullet, the clear-brief bullet's Decisions-ledger sentence and the generic Don't-game-it section. M puts the same seat on Sonnet against Opus and commits nothing. One seat measures the shared text. The brief is an order-inbox card: a 30-second poll, a producer/consumer pair and a clean shutdown, over a worker whose Program.cs registers IOrderStore as a scoped service. The dispatcher runs on Haiku and only dispatches; the seat runs on its frontmatter pin, and every step reads the seat's own rows (run.trace seat - the stream's parent_tool_use_id rows, forwarded with --forward-subagent-text), so the main session naming a trap never counts. scope-per-unit, stopping-token and bounded-channel are the trap list's steps; one-owner (Program.cs on exactly one task's files line - a files: line that names it after a NOT, never, forbidden or except is the forbid the rule asks of the other tasks and is no ownership) and decisions-ledger (a ## Decisions heading, or a Decisions: none - line) are the restatement cut's; oriented-line and status-line are guards that show the seat reached its report. Only the plain level is run. Every step is bound to this fixture (session: false).
